title: Body in White
subtitle: The Complete Guide to Automotive Body Design
author: Subramanian J H

chapters.title: Introduction — The Design of the Automotive Body

topics.title: Preface
concept: This book was written to answer a question every body engineer eventually asks and few books address whole: how is an automotive body actually designed — not analysed after the fact, not admired in cutaway, but designed, decision by decision, from the day a Class-A styling surface arrives to the day a drawing is released with evidence behind every line.

It is written for every level of reader at once. The fresher will find each chapter builds its subject from first principles — what a monocoque is, why a flange is 15 mm, where the loads go. The practising engineer will find the working depth: master sections with standard dimensions, the design methodology for each component from skin surface to inner-panel emboss logic, hinge and gas-stay calculations with their temperature corners, tolerance chains drawn before parts, and the failure modes each chapter’s FMEA tables anchor. The senior reader will find the arguments — steel versus aluminium versus composite decided by method rather than fashion, crumple zones versus survival spaces, the kilogram priced in rupees and now in carbon.

Three questions form the book’s spine, asked of every part in every chapter, always in the same order: Is it functional? Is it manufacturable? Is it assemblable? Everything else — the zone segregation, the closures grammar, the ring logic, the requirement cascade, the gate sequence of Appendix D — is machinery for answering them honestly.

Regulations are treated where design decisions actually meet them: inside the component chapters. The hood chapter carries pedestrian protection; the body side carries side impact; the roof carries crush; the truck cab carries its pendulum trio — with FMVSS, UN-ECE and India’s AIS read together by the superset method (design to the strictest market you will sell in). The book is anchored in the Indian market — its segments, its roads, its duty cycles, its body-builder traditions — and written to be globally applicable, in international English.

A note on numbers: this book is full of them, and they are the point — but dimensional standards, regulation values and cost figures vary by company, market and year. Every such value here is therefore representative and illustrative, and should be confirmed against current standards, datasheets and regulations before professional use. A number without a source is a rumour.

Each component chapter follows the same structure: the design methodology (how to start from the Class-A surface and develop the part, step by step), three to four master sections covering the standard dimensions and the surrounding components, and the design-governing tests and regulations for that component. That designer’s-bible ambition is this book’s differentiator, and Chapter 31’s backdoor is its fullest demonstration.
